title: Durable activation authority ledger
description: Objective: provide the missing durable all-or-none persistence contract for one execution activation without adding ad-hoc SQLite schema. Depends on task-c956fd56f0d24e84a33644934982828f and task-311adb23a3964146a25fa8bddf7123e9. Deliverable: a focused daemon activation-ledger codec/reader/commit adapter that stores one canonical EffectActivationCommitted event containing the claim successor closure plus the runner activation commit and activated budget/slot successors. Derive a dedicated aggregate id from `(effect aggregateId,idempotencyKey)`, always commit it from expected version 0, and use the existing aggregate-head primary key plus globally unique domain-event id set to the grantId to enforce semantic uniqueness. Consumer: task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d. NOT in scope: recovery embargo decisions, HTTP registry wiring, provider launch, schema/table migrations, or constructing claim/activation outcomes. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test.
definitionOfDone: The exact versioned activation record/codec preserves and digest-binds active lease, dimension/attempt-bound ACTIVE provider slot, post-reservation budget view plus ACTIVATED reservation, ACTIVE effect intent, RUNNING attempt, UNUSED grant, predecessor intent/attempt versions, and activation digest.

The commit adapter derives the target aggregate id injectively from `(aggregateId,idempotencyKey)`, requires expected aggregate version 0, uses the grantId as the unique business event id, and appends the decision/event/authority record in one existing @moe/store transaction.

Same-command replay returns the original durable record without rerunning apply; a distinct command for the same aggregate/idempotency pair or the same grantId accepts exactly once and otherwise pins the exact EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT or store uniqueness refusal with zero duplicate events.

The production reader requires exactly one correctly typed event whose payload, derived aggregate id, event id/grant id, versions and digest agree; absent, truncated, extra or malformed evidence returns a typed UNKNOWN/refusal and never reconstructs authority.

Focused concurrency and injected-throw tests assert exact decision disposition/code/layer plus event counts, prove no partial attempt/slot/lease/effect/grant/budget record is observable, and assert every generated race set has positive cardinality.

The focused daemon/store gates pass, a mutation of the production aggregate-id or expected-version guard reddens the named replay/race test, and task-e33747f982e0452a9f9d784fd1cb914d is recorded as the production consumer.
taskRails: Use existing @moe/store aggregate-head, event-id, command-decision and commit-with-apply authorities; do not create SQLite objects or execute daemon-owned ad-hoc DDL.
TDD every behavior; refusal tests pin exact stable code and refusing layer, and zero-authority assertions include a positive accepted control through the production adapter.
Never persist a partial activation tuple or optimistically reconstruct missing bytes; unreadable evidence is UNKNOWN.
Use only public package roots across boundaries; target <=250 physical lines per production source and split before 400.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red for the codec and reader, in a new apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-codec.test.ts. INJECTIVITY: a hand-written table of (aggregateId, idempotencyKey) pairs chosen to collide under naive concatenation — ('a','bc') vs ('ab','c'), separator-bearing inputs, empty-string components — must all derive DISTINCT aggregate ids, and identical inputs must derive an identical id across calls; assert the hand-written pair count. ROUND TRIP: a fully populated record encodes and decodes to a value equal field-for-field with no normalization, and the decoded graph shares no object identity with the input. DIGEST BINDING: mutating any single field of the encoded payload makes the reader refuse — sweep EVERY field mechanically rather than hand-picking three, and assert the swept field count equals the record's own key count so a field added later cannot escape the sweep. READER, which is where authority is most easily invented: exactly one correctly typed event is required, and each of these returns a typed UNKNOWN/refusal with its EXACT code and layer, never a reconstruction — zero events, two events, an event of the wrong type, a payload whose derived aggregate id disagrees with the event's aggregate, an event id that is not the record's grantId, a version disagreement, a digest mismatch, truncated bytes, and a payload carrying an extra key. Pair every refusal case with a POSITIVE accepted control through the same production reader, per task rail 2, so a reader that refuses everything cannot pass the table. Run and record the RED.
implementationPlan.note:

implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-codec.ts plus its `.js` bridge: encode, decode, digest, and the reader. Encoding is canonical — one fixed field order, every variable-length field length-prefixed, so two callers holding the same record produce identical bytes and an identical digest; follow the framing discipline packages/store/src/recovery-install-codec.ts already uses rather than inventing a second one. Decode is a bounded exact-shape parse, never a cast and never a repair: check the digest BEFORE parsing framing so drifted bytes refuse as a mismatch rather than half-interpreting, refuse trailing bytes, and refuse an extra or missing key. The reader takes the events for a derived aggregate and answers with the record only when ALL of these agree: exactly one event, the exact event type, the payload's own derived aggregate id equals the aggregate it was read from, the event id equals the record's grantId, the predecessor intent/attempt versions match the record's, and the digest verifies. Any disagreement returns the typed refusal with its exact code and layer — unreadable evidence is UNKNOWN and never reconstructed from the parts that did parse. Keep under 250 lines; if it crosses, split the reader out rather than trimming the comments.
implementationPlan.note:
NO CHANGE REQUIRED — re-read line by line against the step text and the QA reopen, which explicitly excluded the codec and reader from the rejection ("Codec, reader and contracts are strong"). Re-verified each clause on current bytes rather than on the review's word:

- Canonical: HEADER version frame, field order taken from the frozen ACTIVATION_LEDGER_RECORD_KEYS and never from the caller's key order, every part length-prefixed with a big-endian uint32, digest sealed in the trailing frame. Same discipline as packages/store/src/recovery-install-codec.ts, not a second one.
- Digest checked BEFORE framing is parsed (decode: splitSealed -> digest compare -> header check -> frames), so drifted bytes refuse ACTIVATION_LEDGER_DIGEST_MISMATCH instead of half-interpreting.
- Trailing bytes refused: `cursor.offset !== sealed.body.byteLength` -> BYTES_MALFORMED. Extra/missing key refused twice over — hasExactKeys pins the key count and membership, and the parsed draft is RE-ENCODED and required to reproduce the digest, which is what closes duplicate JSON keys (JSON.parse silently keeps the last) and key-order smuggling.
- Fatal TextDecoder, so mis-framed UTF-8 refuses rather than becoming U+FFFD.
- Reader agrees on all six: exactly one event (0 -> EVIDENCE_ABSENT, >1 -> EVIDENCE_AMBIGUOUS, never "pick one"), exact event type, payload decodes, the payload's OWN derived aggregate id equals both the aggregate read from and event.aggregateId, event.eventId === record.grant.grantId, and both successor versions equal predecessor+1. Every disagreement returns activationLedgerUnknown — there is no branch that answers from the fields that parsed.

SIZE: codec 236 lines, reader 71 — both under the 250 target; the reader was already split out for exactly the reason the step names. Both .js bridges present.

Green under `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-ledger-codec.test.ts src/activation/activation-ledger-reader.test.ts` — exit 0, 23 tests, recorded in step 3. implementationPlan.description: Implement apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ledger-commit.ts plus its `.js` bridge. ONE call to the store's existing commitExpectedVersionDecision, and no ad-hoc SQLite: the durable record IS the event payload, so the decision's own `events` array carries {eventId: grant.grantId, eventType: the record's event-type literal, payload: the canonical bytes}. Do NOT reach for commitWithApply/commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply — CommitApply hands out a raw DatabaseSync and exists for callers who write their own tables, which task rail 1 forbids here; the decision path already gives all three properties this DoD needs, and it gives them from authorities that already exist. Target aggregate id comes from deriveActivationAggregateId, expectedVersion is ALWAYS 0, and the event id is the grantId COPIED from the grant, never minted here. That yields the three uniqueness mechanisms without inventing one: the decision key gives replay (the store skips apply and returns the original decision on a REPLAYED disposition), the aggregate-head primary key with expectedVersion 0 gives EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT for a distinct command on the same pair, and the globally unique domain-event id gives the store's uniqueness refusal for a reused grantId. Map each store outcome to this module's own stable code and layer, preserving the store's upstream code verbatim rather than flattening it. Construct nothing: the claim successors and the activation commit arrive as inputs and are persisted as given. Turn steps 3 and 5 green.
implementationPlan.note:
Adapter already satisfied the step's structural clauses (one commitExpectedVersionDecision, no apply callback — the port cannot name one, expectedVersion pinned 0, eventId COPIED from grant.grantId, aggregate from deriveActivationAggregateId, store codes preserved verbatim in storeCode, nothing constructed). This pass fixes the BLOCKING defect at the old line 138: the ok return built record/digest from the caller's input on EVERY path, REPLAYED included.

NEW `answerReplayed(store, aggregateId, candidateDigest)`, taken on `response.disposition === "REPLAYED"` only:
1. `store.readEvents(aggregateId)` inside try/catch -> refuseThrown, so a store fault on the read is refused with the same vocabulary as a fault on the commit. This is the first production call to the port's `readEvents`, which QA correctly noted was declared and never used.
2. `readActivationLedgerRecord(aggregateId, events)` — the SAME production reader a recovery caller uses, so the replay path gets exactly one event, exact event type, digest-before-framing, payload-derives-to-this-aggregate, eventId === grantId and both predecessor+1 checks. A reader refusal is propagated VERBATIM as its UNKNOWN; there is no branch that turns unverifiable evidence into an ok result.
3. Candidate compared to durable by CANONICAL DIGEST, not field by field: the encoding is deterministic, so one digest covers all twelve fields and cannot silently omit the one that drifted. Disagreement -> ACTIVATION_LEDGER_REPLAY_DIVERGED, outcome REFUSED, storeCode NULL (no store call refused).
4. Agreement -> ok carrying `sealed.record`, which came out of DECODE of the stored payload. The caller's object never reaches the return on this path.

COMMITTED path deliberately still answers from `encoded`: the store just wrote those exact bytes, so re-reading would prove nothing the append did not. That asymmetry is what keeps the COMMITTED-path spy assertion (`calls === ["commitExpectedVersionDecision"]`) meaningful — reading unconditionally would satisfy the replay assertion while destroying that one.

No cycle introduced: reader imports codec+contracts, commit imports codec+contracts+reader.

implementationPlan.description: Mutation drills, the ones DoD 6 names plus the ones that protect the reader. For each: sha256 first, edit with the Edit tool, confirm the anchor matched once, run only the named test, reverse the edit, confirm the sha256 is restored — never git checkout, which reverts to HEAD and would destroy uncommitted work in this shared worktree. D1 (named by DoD 6): replace the framed aggregate-id derivation with a bare concatenation — the injectivity table reddens on the colliding pair, proving the framing is load-bearing rather than decorative. D2 (named by DoD 6): change expectedVersion from 0 to the observed version — the distinct-command conflict case and the race case redden, because a second activation would then be accepted onto the same aggregate. D3: mint a fresh event id instead of copying the grantId — the grantId-reuse case reddens. D4: have the reader accept the first event when two are present — the exactly-one case reddens. D5: skip the digest check in the reader — the per-field mutation sweep reddens; confirm it reddens on MANY fields, since a sweep that reddens on only one has quietly stopped sweeping. Read every failure message and confirm it names the assertion the drill targets; a red for the wrong reason means the drill is broken, not that the guard is proven.

Gate, review, commit. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm --filter @moe/store test` fresh in the foreground and keep the verbatim tail; subtract the step-1 baseline and confirm no new failing path intersects the owned paths, disclosing any foreign red verbatim rather than fabricating green. Root `pnpm test` excludes apps/**, so the daemon leg is the only one gating this work. Re-measure every new production file with `grep -c ''` against the 250 target. Adversarial review over the owned diff: is any SQLite object or DDL created (rail 1 forbids it); is any claim or activation outcome CONSTRUCTED rather than persisted as given; can a partial tuple be observed on any failure path; does any refusal flatten the store's upstream code; is the aggregate-id derivation injective for adversarial inputs including empty components and separator-bearing ids; does the reader ever answer from the fields that did parse; and does the record's field set still cover every fact DoD 1 enumerates — count the nouns in that sentence against the interface, because an eight-fact list is easy to ship with seven. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, and this is the plan's central decision: using commitWithApply / commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply. CommitApply (packages/store/src/event-ledger-transaction.ts:30-39) hands the callback a raw DatabaseSync and exists for callers who write their OWN tables inside the commit transaction — exactly what task rail 1 forbids ('do not create SQLite objects or execute daemon-owned ad-hoc DDL'). The plain decision path already delivers all three properties this DoD needs from authorities that exist: the decision key gives replay, the aggregate head with expectedVersion 0 gives the conflict, and the globally unique domain-event id gives the grantId uniqueness. The durable record is therefore the EVENT PAYLOAD, not a side table. REJECTED: a second uniqueness mechanism of this task's own invention — two are already there and both are store-owned. REJECTED: re-declaring the persisted record's field types locally; every field is typed from the producing package's public root so a producer change is a compile error here rather than a silent divergence in durable bytes. REJECTED: planning against the b64e336/50c492a/284d5dd bytes the reopen note names — they predate two QA rejections and a re-plan, and the note explicitly says re-measure; step 1 does, and the five-record shape is confirmed unchanged on current bytes. REJECTED: a separate reader module up front — decode and cross-check are one responsibility; the plan says to split only if the file crosses 250 lines.

MEASURED at HEAD ab45234, 2026-08-14. NOTE the board moved twice during this planning session, which is why every claim below carries its command.

PRODUCER SURFACE, RE-MEASURED PER THE BLOCK'S OWN CONDITION. apps/daemon/src/work/work-kernel.ts:149 — ClaimSuccessors is exactly five readonly fields: lease: LeaseRecord, providerSlot: ProviderSlotReservation, budgetReservation: ReservationRecord, budgetView: BudgetAvailableView, effectIntent: EffectIntent. This MATCHES the pre-rejection description, so the reopen note's worry that the shape might have changed is resolved: it did not. WorkGranted at :177 carries `successors: ClaimSuccessors`. task-311adb23 is DONE; its final fix was routing liveClaims array elements through the same detach recursion as every other section, which changes parsing, not this shape.

ACTIVATION HALF, WHICH THIS TASK PERSISTS AND MUST NOT CONSTRUCT. packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-activation.ts:59 ActivationCommit {activationVersion, intent, attempt, grant, activationDigest}; :67 ActivationOutcome ACTIVATED{commit} | REFUSED{failure}. effect-kernel.ts:201 AttemptSlice {attemptId, aggregateId, intentId, state, version}; :224 ActivationGrant {grantId, intentId, wrapperIdentity, state, version} — so the grantId this task uses as the event id is produced upstream by deriveGrantId and is COPIED, never minted. packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:73/93 publish activateProviderSlot (the sole RESERVED->ACTIVE transition, binding the attempt) and activateReservation (binds an attempt, moves NO units) — the ACTIVE attempt-bound slot and the ACTIVATED reservation come from there.

GAP OPEN. `grep -rn "EffectActivationCommitted|activation-ledger|ActivationLedger" --include=*.ts apps/ packages/` returns ZERO. apps/daemon/src has no activation/ directory (bootstrap, coordination, documents, goals, http, identity, orchestrator, planning, projections, recovery, review, work).

EDGES PRESENT. apps/daemon/package.json declares @moe/contracts, @moe/coordination, @moe/core, @moe/mcp, @moe/review, @moe/runner, @moe/scheduler, @moe/store, all workspace:*. The compiled bare-specifier probe in step 1 is still required by the rail; the manifest line is not sufficient on its own.

STORE MECHANICS. sqlite-event-store.ts:267/274 expose commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply and commitWithApply; decision-ledger-transaction.ts:192 shows apply runs ONLY when effectDisposition is EFFECTS_COMMITTED, which is precisely why a replay cannot rerun it — that is a property of the store, not something this task must re-implement. domain_events.event_id is UNIQUE (sqlite-schema-manifest.ts) and aggregate_heads.aggregate_id is the primary key, which is where the two uniqueness guarantees actually live.

CANONICAL-BYTES PRECEDENT to copy rather than reinvent: packages/store/src/recovery-install-codec.ts — fixed field order, length-prefixed variable fields, digest checked before framing is parsed, trailing bytes refused.
planningNotes.risks:
1. A NON-INJECTIVE AGGREGATE ID IS THE SILENT CATASTROPHE. Concatenating (aggregateId, idempotencyKey) lets ('a','bc') and ('ab','c') land on one aggregate, where expectedVersion 0 then makes the SECOND activation look like a duplicate of the first — a wrong accept and a wrong refuse from the same bug. Frame the inputs, and drill it (D1).
2. THE APPLY CALLBACK IS A TRAP. It is right there, it takes a DatabaseSync, and using it would violate rail 1 while appearing to satisfy 'one transaction'. The decision path already covers replay, conflict and uniqueness.
3. REPLAY MUST NOT RERUN APPLY — assert it with a counter, not by inspecting the disposition alone; the disposition can read REPLAYED while a side effect still fired if anything is ever moved into the caller.
4. THE PER-FIELD DIGEST SWEEP CAN GO VACUOUS. Assert the swept field count equals the record's own key count, or a field added next quarter is silently unbound. Drill D5 must redden on MANY fields.
5. A REFUSAL TABLE WITHOUT A POSITIVE CONTROL PASSES FOR A READER THAT REFUSES EVERYTHING. Rail 2 requires the accepted control through the same production adapter.
6. HELD SQLITE HANDLE KILLS THE VITEST WORKER. On Windows an open handle makes the temp-dir cleanup throw EPERM and the run dies with zero test output, reading as a native crash. Open and close inside each `it`, and close in the race worker's finally BEFORE posting its result.
7. FLATTENING THE STORE'S UPSTREAM CODE loses the distinction between an expected-version conflict and a uniqueness violation, which DoD 3 requires to be separately assertable. Preserve it verbatim.
8. COUNT THE NOUNS IN DoD 1. It enumerates eight facts plus versions plus digest; an interface that ships seven of them typechecks and passes every test written against itself.
9. SHARED WORKTREE. .moe/**, packages/store/**, packages/contracts/** and adapters/** carry other agents' uncommitted work. Never git add -A, never stash, never reset; git add the six new files explicitly before committing by pathspec.

issues.description: BLOCKING. The ok return builds record/digest from the CALLER'S input on every path including REPLAYED, so a replay can describe an activation never committed. The port already declares readEvents and production never calls it. Fix either: (a) on REPLAYED resolve the record from the derived aggregate via readActivationLedgerRecord and return THAT, refusing on disagreement; or (b) cross-check decision.businessEventIds against the grantId. Needs a new stable code.

BLOCKING. The replay test commits input() twice, so expect(second.record).toEqual(first.record) holds by construction and cannot fail whatever the adapter returns. Add a replay case with same key and same requestBytes but a record field drifted OUTSIDE the store's request identity - grant.grantId is sharpest, it is the durable event id. Assert the returned record carries the DURABLE grantId, or that it refuses with exact code and layer. Prove it reddens by mutating the REPLAYED branch.

NON-BLOCKING note; production is correct. COLLIDING_PAIRS calls its rows separator-bearing but smuggles ':' while the real separator is '|'. I drilled it: dropping the length prefixes while keeping '|' leaves all 12 codec tests GREEN. True bare-concat does redden (expected 5 to be 10), so the guard is load-bearing; file restored byte-exact, sha256 verified. Add one pair whose component holds a literal '|'.

rejectionHistory.reason:
DoD 3 fails on the REPLAYED path: the adapter returns the CALLER'S record as durable authority, not the original durable record. Reproduced against a real file-backed store.

REPRO (probe written, run, deleted; owned tree left byte-clean):
first commit record(); second commit same key, same requestBytes, only grant.grantId drifted to "grant-NEVER-COMMITTED" ->
  ok=true | disposition=REPLAYED | returnedGrantId=grant-NEVER-COMMITTED | durableEventId=grant-0001 | eventCount=1
The adapter reports success and hands back a grant that is not in the store. Epic rail 4 and task rail 3: unverifiable evidence must be UNKNOWN, never optimistically reconstructed.

WHY THE STORE DOES NOT CATCH IT: decision-ledger-transaction.ts:126 compares only requestSha256, and store-digests.ts:82-95 hashes identity version, projectId, principalId, commandId, commandKind, targetAggregateId, expectedVersion, requestBytes. The adapter pins commandKind and expectedVersion constant and derives targetAggregateId from record.effectIntent.{aggregateId,idempotencyKey} alone. Lease, providerSlot, budgetReservation, budgetView, attempt, grant, both predecessor versions and activationDigest are ALL outside the replay identity. (Drift that CHANGES the derived aggregate does refuse with IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT - I probed that first.)

WHY THE TEST CANNOT SEE IT: commit.test.ts:117-138 passes input() twice, so second.record equals first.record by construction - a transcript, not a discriminator.

GATES I RE-RAN: daemon typecheck exit 0; @moe/store test exit 0 (469); daemon test exit 1 on ONE foreign failure, src/recovery/restore-controller.test.ts, NOT attributable to this diff (activation-ledger has zero references outside apps/daemon/src/activation/; red traces to identity/genesis-recovery-binding.ts landed after baseline ab45234 by another task). Owned-path intersection empty - disclosed, not held against you. See issues for one non-blocking note.
